replies:
Trainee — your career agent. I'll run a mock interview for a financial analyst role. I'll ask the first interview question now; answer as you would in the room (short, specific, with a result). I'll score it, give one concrete improvement, then ask the next question. Ready?

Question 1: "Walk me through your resume — highlight the experiences that make you a strong fit for this financial analyst role."

Score: 2/10.
One improvement: add a result metric (how much time or error you reduced, how accurate the forecast was versus actuals, or a % improvement). Next question — "Tell me about a time you influenced a cross-functional team to change course."

Honest score: 2/10.

Why: your answer is a high-level method, not an interview response. Interviewers listen for a specific Situation, what you were asked to do (Task), the concrete Actions you took, and a measurable Result. Right now you:
- gave process only (build a three-statement model, check against comps),
- named no context (which company or problem, timeline, stakeholders),
- did not describe your role or specific steps (what drivers, what assumptions, what tests, what tools),
- gave no outcome (impact on decisions, accuracy, time saved, $ or %).
How to fix it: rewrite using STAR in 2–3 sentences:
1) One line: Situation + Task (context and your responsibility).
2) One line: Actions — specific steps, key assumptions, tools, and how you validated.
3) One line: Result — a measurable outcome (%, $ impact, time saved, decision changed).
Example rewrite to edit with your real facts:
"At [Company], we needed a 12-month forecast after a 10% quarter-over-quarter revenue drop (Situation). I led the forecast (Task). I built a three-statement model driven by SKU-level sales drivers, stress-tested downside scenarios against three public comps, and adjusted marketing and launch timing assumptions after stakeholder review (Action). The model improved forecast accuracy by [X]% versus the prior model and led leadership to delay a product launch, saving [$/%] in expected burn over 6 months (Result)."
One concrete next step: pick one real project and rewrite your answer with the exact company, dates, numbers and your role; I’ll score the new version and give one tweak. Which project will you use?

You don't have any Lincoln International items on file yet. The one step that starts a tracked prep is to paste the interview invite (or tell me the date/time, format and who you meet) so I can save it and tailor prep.

Prep now: quick brief, likely questions, scored answer framework, 10-point plan, and a mock first question.
Brief (what matters in a final analyst round)
- Lincoln International is a mid-market investment bank focused on M&A/advisory for middle-market companies; finals check technical fit, deal experience, fit with long hours/analyst teamwork, and communication with senior bankers and clients.
- Interviewers will probe your technical accounting/modeling ability, deal-process knowledge, behavioral fit (teamwork, ownership, pressure), and case or modeling questions. Expect 1:1s with senior bankers and a partner or director.
Top question types to prepare
1) Technical accounting & valuation: walkthrough a 3-statement model, how to build a DCF, how to value a company, levered vs unlevered FCF, WACC components, LBO basics.
2) Deal experience / transactions: talk through deals you worked on—your role, contributions, challenges, results (numbers).
3) Behavioral / fit: teamwork, failure/conflict, why banking, why Lincoln, where you add value, long hours.
4) Case / modeling test: short case or take-home, quick math, reading an IM excerpt, or live modeling.
5) Market / sector awareness: why their sectors, recent Lincoln deal you like, and why it mattered.
Score-driven answer structure I’ll use when I score your practice answers
- Situation: 1 sentence context with numbers
- Task: what you had to do / your goal
- Action: concrete actions you took (tools, models, outreach) — first person, specific
- Result: quantitative outcome or clear resolution; if no number, what changed, what you learned
10-point final-round prep plan (do these, in order)
1) Read the invite & note format + interviewers (paste it here so I can save it). (I can record it when you paste.)
2) Pick 3 deals you know best (ideally that match Lincoln sectors); prepare 1-paragraph story for each: your role, tasks, outcome, numbers.
3) Review core technicals: build a quick 3-statement link and DCF outline (walkthrough aloud) and memorize WACC inputs and common multiples.
4) Prepare 4 behavioral stories (teamwork, leadership, mistake, motivation for IB) using the STAR structure.
5) Rehearse 6 “why Lincoln” lines: 2 about their culture/size, 2 about deal work, 2 personal fit (hours, learning).
6) Read 2 recent Lincoln announcements or deal blurbs (I can help find them if you want) and be ready to explain one.
7) Do 2 timed mental math drills (multiplication, margins, growth %, quick IRR intuition).
8) Run one mock interview with me: I’ll ask a final-round question and score you.
9) Prepare 2 smart questions to ask each interviewer (one technical, one about their work/style).
10) Logistics: print copies of your resume, confirm travel/tech set-up, rest and sleep schedule.
Common final-round questions and short model answers (practice these)
- Tell me about a recent deal you worked on.
Model: “We advised [client] ([$X] revenue). My role: built the 3-statement model and performed comps/precedent analysis. I identified [issue], adjusted EBITDA by [$Y] via [assumption change], and supported the management presentation that led to a signed LOI within 6 weeks.” (Add numbers and personal actions.)
- Walk me through a DCF.
Model: Start with forecasted unlevered FCF from the income statement and working capital, discount by WACC (explain components: risk-free, beta, ERP, capital structure), calculate terminal value (gordon or exit multiple), sum PVs to enterprise value, adjust for net debt to get equity value per share.
- Tell me about a time you missed a deadline.
Model: Brief situation, what caused it, corrective steps you took (communicated, reprioritized, worked extra hours), and the result and the permanent process change you implemented.

Mock start: first question now
“Walk me through a basic 3-statement model and where you’d look for stress-test risks on the balance sheet.”
Answer aloud in one or two paragraphs and I’ll score it on structure, evidence and specificity, then give one concrete improvement and the next question.

Saved: nothing yet from your invite — paste the invite (or give date, format, interviewer names) and I’ll record it and tailor the prep. Is that right?

You don't have any applications or a posting queued on file yet. The one step that starts this is: tell me which job (paste the posting link or its title and company) you want me to prepare an application for.
Default I will assume the employer uses a standard careers form with these common fields and that you'll attach a resume PDF and a short tailored cover note where the form allows free text. Below I list, exactly and in order, the fields I will fill for the first posting you pick, with what I will put in each field from what I know and what I'll ask you to supply or confirm where needed. I assume US-style names for fields; if the posting shows additional or different fields, I'll follow those instead.

What I will submit (field by field)
1) Job applied to
- What I fill: the posting title and the employer name, exactly as on the posting.
- Where it comes from: the posting you give me.
2) Location
- What I fill: the city/state or "Remote" as the posting requires.
- If you have a location preference on file I will use that; otherwise I'll ask you.

3) Full name
- What I fill: I will use the name you type when I ask "What name and email should go at the top of your resume?" If you haven't given it, I'll ask before preparing.

4) Email address
- What I fill: the email you give me to use for applications (I won't guess or use account email).
- I will ask you if not provided.

5) Phone number
- What I fill: the phone number you provide. If you leave it blank, I will leave the field blank for you to fill on the employer form.
6) Resume / CV upload
- What I attach: a PDF resume. If you have one already confirmed on file, I'll use that; otherwise I'll ask you to paste or upload your resume.
- Note: I will tailor the resume only from your confirmed facts; if you want tailoring from a draft resume paste, paste it now.
7) Cover letter / Application note (short)
- What I fill: a concise tailored paragraph (under 200 words) that explains your fit for the role, pulled from your confirmed facts and the posting's required skills. Where I lack facts, I'll insert [brackets] for you to confirm/edit.
- Example placeholder I would write: "[Two-sentence summary of your top relevant achievement], plus [one technical skill or qualification matching the posting]. Available to start [earliest start date]."

8) LinkedIn profile (optional)
- What I fill: the LinkedIn URL you provide. If you don't provide one, I leave it blank.
9) Work authorization / Visa status
- What I fill: the status you supply (e.g., US citizen, GC, H-1B, need sponsorship). I will ask you for this if not on file.

10) Earliest start date / notice period
- What I fill: the date or notice period you give (e.g., two weeks, 30 days).

11) Salary expectation (if asked)
- What I fill: the exact range or number you give me, or "not listed" / "negotiable" if you prefer. I will not invent pay numbers.

12) Portfolio or code links (if requested)
- What I fill: any URLs you supply (portfolio, GitHub, project links). I will not guess or create content.
13) Screening questions (yes/no or short answers)
- What I fill: I will answer each screening question truthfully from facts confirmed on file or from what you tell me now. If a question needs a short narrative (e.g., "Describe your experience with X"), I'll draft a 1–3 sentence answer referencing your confirmed facts and mark anything missing with [brackets] for you to fill.

14) Uploads or attachments beyond resume (certificates, transcripts)
- What I fill: I will attach files you supply; otherwise leave blank.

15) EEO / voluntary demographic questions
- What I fill: I will leave these blank unless you tell me exactly what to answer.
16) Additional comments / message to recruiter
- What I fill: a short closing line (example: "Thanks for considering my application — I look forward to the chance to discuss how I can help [company] with [skill].") I'll draft it and leave any bracketed specifics for you to confirm.
What I will not do without your explicit answers and approvals
- I will not invent your name, email, phone, visa status, salary expectations, or earliest start date.
- I will not submit the application; I will prepare the card for you to review and approve in the Trainee extension (or, if you ask, prepare the exact text you will paste into the employer form).
- I will not attach or invent portfolio items or certificates.
Assumptions I made to prepare this checklist
- Employer uses a standard careers form; if the posting uses an unusual portal (single-click profile, third-party assessment, or requires a code), I will change the fields to match the posting once you give me the posting link.
- You want a resume PDF and a short tailored note attached.
- You have not yet provided contact, resume or visa facts in this conversation.
Next step
Paste the job posting link or the exact job title and company you want me to prepare the first application for, and give the name and email you want on your resume. I'll list every exact field the posting asks for (read from the posting) and show you the precise text I will put into each field, with [brackets] where I need your input. Is that the posting you want me to start with?
